note: Canonical model input contract. Java FeatureSchema, the training pipeline and the inference service must all agree with this file; NeuralSchemaContractTest and ml/tests/test_schema.py both pin it. Values are window-local: derived deltas at window index 0 have no predecessor inside the window and are masked. Mask channels follow all value channels, in declaration order of the nullable values, named <NAME>_MASK. Absolute positions, entity/transaction/session identifiers, protocol version, held item, player identity, dataset collection metadata (scenario, assistStrength, clientFamily, configuration) and Grim check evidence are deliberately absent: identity and recording conditions must not be learnable, and deterministic check output must not become the label the model copies. A channel may declare a monotone transform applied before clipping; the clip bounds are stated in transformed units.

values.name: CROSSHAIR_ON_TARGET
values.unit: 1 when the look ray enters the target box

values.name: CROSSHAIR_HIT_HEIGHT
values.unit: fraction of target box height where the look ray enters

values.name: CENTER_AIM_ERROR
values.unit: deg between look direction and target box centre

values.name: GRID_RESIDUAL_YAW
values.unit: counts from the nearest whole count

values.name: GRID_RESIDUAL_PITCH
values.unit: counts from the nearest whole count

derivations.rotationTargetAlignment: cos angle between (DELTA_YAW,DELTA_PITCH) and (targetAngularVelocityYaw,targetAngularVelocityPitch); unknown when either norm < 1e-6
derivations.targetAngularRadius: degrees(atan2(0.5 * max(TARGET_MAX_X-TARGET_MIN_X, TARGET_MAX_Z-TARGET_MIN_Z), DISTANCE_TO_TARGET)) when DISTANCE_TO_TARGET > 1e-6
derivations.sameTarget(t): t > 0 within the window AND TARGET_PRESENT[t]=1 AND TARGET_PRESENT[t-1]=1 AND TARGET_ENTITY_ID[t]=TARGET_ENTITY_ID[t-1] AND TARGET_SWITCH[t]=0 AND SEGMENT_START[t]=0
derivations.TICKS_SINCE_TARGET_SWITCH: raw field, but the -1 sentinel written when no target is tracked counts as unknown; the known value is then transformed with log1p before clipping
derivations.aimErrorFrame(t-1): e = (wrap180(YAW[t-1] - TARGET_YAW[t-1]), PITCH[t-1] - TARGET_PITCH[t-1]), the aim error the player's rotation d = (DELTA_YAW[t], DELTA_PITCH[t]) responds to; usable when sameTarget(t) and |e| >= 1 degree
derivations.rotationCorrectionGain: -(d . e) / |e|^2 over aimErrorFrame(t-1): the fraction of last sample's aim error the rotation removed. A smoothing aim assist (yaw += (target - yaw) * k) holds it near k; a hand does not
derivations.rotationOffAxis: (d_yaw * e_pitch - d_pitch * e_yaw) / |e|^2 over aimErrorFrame(t-1): the rotation perpendicular to the error, in the same units. Assisted rotation runs straight at the target; yaw-odd
derivations.look(t): (-sin(yaw) * cos(pitch), -sin(pitch), cos(yaw) * cos(pitch)) with yaw = radians(YAW), pitch = radians(PITCH)
derivations.targetBox(t): [TARGET_MIN_*, TARGET_MAX_*]; usable when TARGET_PRESENT=1 and every box, eye and rotation field is finite
derivations.crosshairOnTarget: slab test of the ray eye + s*look, s >= 0, against targetBox: 1 when max(entry, 0) <= exit, else 0; unknown when targetBox is unusable. An axis with |look| < 1e-9 misses unless eye lies within that slab. Pure geometry of one box, not a world raycast
derivations.crosshairHitHeight: (eye.y + max(entry, 0) * look.y - TARGET_MIN_Y) / (TARGET_MAX_Y - TARGET_MIN_Y) when crosshairOnTarget = 1 and the box height > 1e-6; otherwise unknown
derivations.centerAimError: degrees(acos(clamp(look . c / |c|, -1, 1))) with c = box centre - eye; unknown when targetBox is unusable or |c| < 1e-6
derivations.rotationCountsYaw: DELTA_YAW / MOUSE_GRID_YAW when MOUSE_GRID_YAW > 1e-6: the rotation in mouse counts, which does not depend on the player's sensitivity
derivations.gridResidualYaw: |rotationCountsYaw - rint(rotationCountsYaw)| (round half to even, Java Math.rint / numpy rint): 0 for a rotation a mouse can produce, up to 0.5 for one it cannot

windows.attack: anchored on a sample whose ATTACK=1; attackBefore samples before it, the attack sample, attackAfter samples after it. Complete tick ids only, no segment boundary after index 0.
windows.continuous: the last sequenceLength consecutive samples with no segment boundary after index 0.

transforms.log1p: natural log(1 + x), defined for x >= 0; unknown stays unknown and a negative input is unknown

versionHistory.2: TICKS_SINCE_TARGET_SWITCH changed from a raw sample count clipped at 200 to log1p(samples) clipped at 12. At the old bound the channel was constant for roughly three quarters of sampled windows (p50 = p99 = max = 200), so the clip discarded the dominant regime rather than a tail. log1p keeps full resolution in the first samples after a target switch, where the signal is, and compresses the long tail instead of erasing it. Bundles built for version 1 are rejected: the channel means something different now.
versionHistory.3: ROTATION_CORRECTION_GAIN and ROTATION_OFF_AXIS added after AIM_ERROR_RATIO: the player's rotation expressed in the frame of the previous aim error. Derived from raw fields that already existed, so raw schema 1 recordings are unchanged and usable; bundles built for schema 2 must be retrained.
versionHistory.4: CROSSHAIR_ON_TARGET, CROSSHAIR_HIT_HEIGHT, CENTER_AIM_ERROR and CENTER_AIM_ERROR_RATIO added after ROTATION_OFF_AXIS: where the crosshair actually is relative to the target box. AIM_ERROR_* measure the angle to the box point nearest the eyes, which cannot tell a crosshair resting inside the hitbox from one just outside it, and says nothing about where inside the box an assist parks the aim. Derived from raw fields that already existed (YAW, PITCH, PLAYER_*, EYE_HEIGHT, TARGET_MIN/MAX_*), so raw schema 1 recordings stay usable; bundles built for schema 3 must be retrained.
versionHistory.5: Raw schema 2 adds MOUSE_GRID_YAW and MOUSE_GRID_PITCH, the degrees per mouse count Grim's AimProcessor estimates; raw schema 1 recordings still load, with both unknown. ROTATION_COUNTS_YAW/PITCH and GRID_RESIDUAL_YAW/PITCH are added after CENTER_AIM_ERROR_RATIO. Degrees per sample mix behaviour with sensitivity, so the model could learn a player's sensitivity instead of how they aim; counts remove it. A rotation that is not a whole number of counts cannot come from a mouse, which is the classic trace of injected rotation. Bundles built for schema 4 must be retrained.
